 Miami’s Mario Cristobal shares every reason why Darian Mensah is so special ahead of Pitt clash
 Mensah has been a spark plug this season for the Miami football team. The Hurricanes head coach knows that he is special.
 By Benjamin Adducchio • Updated Oct 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM ET • 2 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Miami (FL) football team hopes to return to the College Football Playoff in 2026. Miami head coach Mario Cristobal is sharing some reasons why his quarterback Darian Mensah is such a special player . The Hurricanes are getting ready to play Pittsburgh on Saturday.
 “Darian Mensah has a relentless mentality.. He demands the most of himself and his teammates.. He's just different and we're blessed to have him on our football team,” Cristobal said while speaking on ESPN to Pat McAfee.
 "Darian Mensah has a relentless mentality..
 He demands the most of himself and his teammates..
 He's just different and we're blessed to have him on our football team" ~ @coach_cristobal #CollegeGameDay pic.twitter.com/IWvJQrEL3v 
 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 24, 2026 
 The Hurricanes are off to a great start to the season. Miami enters Saturday's game with the Panthers, holding a 6-0 record.
 Mensah has posted 1,764 passing yards this season, with just one interception. He has thrown 18 touchdown passes for Miami.
 Mensah is ready to face a very stringent Pittsburgh defense.
 “I think their run defense is, I think, number one in the country,” Mensah said, per the school. “Physical, good d-line, really good third-down package, so, yeah, we’ve got to come prepared. That’s what stands out.”
 The Hurricanes reached the CFP in 2025, and advanced all the way to the national championship game. Even though Miami lost that game to Indiana, the Hurricanes nearly pulled off the upset. Miami clearly carried a lot of momentum into this campaign, and it is showing so far.
 Article Continues Below Miami is preparing to play a hungry Pitt team on Saturday, that looks to pull off the upset.
 “Watching their offense, they have two good quarterbacks that are good at both running and [passing]. We’re just getting ready for everything,” Hurricanes defensive lineman Armondo Blount said. “They’ve got a good team. Good o-linemen. Physical team. We know they’re coming down here to play.”
 Miami is currently sitting at the top of the ACC standings. The Hurricanes are 4-0 in the ACC. Pittsburgh enters the game with a 2-2 conference record.
 Miami and Pitt play Saturday at 12:00 ET. The Panthers enter the game with a 5-2 record.
